definition: Infidelity is the rejection of the central beliefs of a religion, especially Christianity in this historical usage. It refers to doctrinal unbelief rather than moral wrongdoing, and it is treated as a kind of skepticism without being the same as atheism, agnosticism, deism, naturalism, or rationalism.
